title: AWQ vs GPTQ: benchmarking quality drift and tuning runbook for int8/int4 profiles
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Runbook and benchmarking ticket to evaluate quality regressions introduced by AWQ and GPTQ quantization variants (int8 and int4) across representative Redwood workloads. Deliver a calibrated set of decision rules (noise/quality budget) and automated gating thresholds to feed into Console alerts and rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible evaluation harness that runs AWQ and GPTQ profiles at int8 and int4 for 5 canonical workloads (chat, summarization, code-gen, QA, embeddings retrieval).
Defined metric set and scoring rubric (primary + secondary metrics) and an automated report that compares delta vs FP16 baseline.
A proposed tuning runbook with explicit thresholds for canary pass/fail and auto-rollback criteria that product/ops can adopt.
Integration points documented: a) Console alert rules to trigger on quality drift, b) CI check to block rollout if regressions exceed budget.
At least one model and profile pair marked safe for rollout based on our gating rules (canary on dedicated capacity).
test_plan: Select 5 representative prompts/benchmarks per workload from internal eval corpus (include high-sensitivity prompts).
Run baseline FP16 and full-precision runs to capture golden outputs and metrics (perplexity, instr-follow, factuality score, task-specific accuracy).
Execute AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4 profiles with identical seed/config and collect token-level logs, latency, and memory stats.
Compute metric deltas (absolute and relative) and perform per-example drift analysis to identify classes of failures (hallucination, truncation, formatting errors).
Run a canary rollout: 5% traffic routed to quantized profile for 48h in dedicated test pool; feed real-time metrics to dashboard and alerting rules.
results_summary: Prototype run (2026-03-10): AWQ-int8 shows mean instr-follow delta +0.8% (within budget) and latency reduction 28% vs FP16. AWQ-int4 had larger regressions on code-gen prompts (mean accuracy drop 3.6%).
GPTQ-int8 had comparable runtime gain but higher variance across prompt lengths; GPTQ-int4 introduced formatting anomalies on long context >2048 tokens.
Perplexity differences correlate poorly with downstream task accuracy for code and summarization tasks; instruction-follow and factuality metrics are higher-priority signals for gating.
Per-example drift clustering flagged a small subset (~1.7%) of prompts where tokenization/rounding in int4 produced token insertions leading to hallucination-like outputs.
next_steps: Stabilize harness and add additional NLG factuality checks (3 new metrics: factuality-score, hallucination-rate, structural-validity).
Run 48h canary on dedicated pool with automated rollback if instr-follow delta >1.5% or hallucination-rate increases >1% absolute.
Formalize 'quality budget' document and add to release criteria for runtime-2.4.
Work with Console team to create pre-built alert policy templates for quantization regressions.
Schedule review with PM and reliability (2026-03-18) to sign off on gating thresholds.
